Clearance-rate decomposition and Simpson's paradox

Source: R/pol.R
clrsmp.Rd

Splits the change in an aggregate clearance rate between two periods, areas or services (A and B) into a rate effect, from each offence type clearing more or less, and a mix effect, from the workload moving between types that clear at different rates (Kitagawa's decomposition). The two always add up to the change. When every type clears better in B and the aggregate still falls, the fall is all mix: Simpson's paradox, and the reason an aggregate clearance rate cannot be read as performance without the split by type. See proof("clrsmp").

Usage

clrsmp(clra, reca, clrb, recb)

Arguments

clra

Offences cleared in A, by type: non-negative numbers, optionally named.

reca

Offences recorded in A, by type: positive numbers, same length.

clrb

Offences cleared in B, by type: non-negative numbers, same length.

recb

Offences recorded in B, by type: positive numbers, same length.

Value

A list. parts, a data frame with one row per type: part, ratea, rateb (clearance rates), sharea, shareb (shares of the recorded workload), rateeff and mixeff. total, a named numeric vector: ratea, rateb (aggregate rates), change, rateeff, mixeff (with change = rateeff + mixeff), up and down (types whose rate rose or fell) and simpson: 2 when every type moved one way and the aggregate the other, 1 when the aggregate change and the rate effect differ in sign, 0 otherwise.

Details

Each part's mix term is measured from the mean of the two aggregate rates, so a part's term is negative when work moved toward a part that clears below average; the centre changes how the mix effect is shared among the parts, never its total.

References

Kitagawa, E. M. (1955). Components of a difference between two rates. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 50(272), 1168-1194. doi:10.1080/01621459.1955.10501299

Examples

# both types clear better in B, yet the aggregate falls
clrsmp(clra = c(minor = 90, serious = 20), reca = c(100, 50),
       clrb = c(19, 60), recb = c(20, 140))
#> $parts
#>      part ratea     rateb    sharea shareb    rateeff     mixeff
#> 1   minor   0.9 0.9500000 0.6666667  0.125 0.01979167 -0.1687066
#> 2 serious   0.4 0.4285714 0.3333333  0.875 0.01726190 -0.1079303
#> 
#> $total
#>       ratea       rateb      change     rateeff      mixeff          up 
#>  0.73333333  0.49375000 -0.23958333  0.03705357 -0.27663690  2.00000000 
#>        down     simpson 
#>  0.00000000  2.00000000 
#>
